author: Jiawei Zhang
task_instruction: Andrew Chen has been anxious about the upcoming suppression hearing in his DUI case, and he needs a thorough update letter that explains the strategy clearly. Open matter M-2024-112 for State v. Chen and review the case notes on the breathalyzer calibration challenge, the field sobriety test suppression arguments, and any procedural developments. Check the document vault for the calibration records, police reports, and any correspondence with DDA Jennifer Walsh from the Santa Clara County DA's office. Search for recent DUI suppression decisions in California courts that address breathalyzer reliability and field sobriety test admissibility -- Andrew will want to know how courts have been treating these challenges. Pull the full opinion for the most analogous decision so we can reference the evidentiary standards and the arguments that succeeded. Note that Judge Gregory McBride is presiding and has a reputation for careful scrutiny of forensic evidence. Draft the update letter through the drafting system, covering the suppression hearing timeline, our challenge to the BAC results, the field sobriety test issues, and next steps. Draft the completed work product using the legal drafting tools and save it to the matter file. Add a note to the matter file logging that the draft has been completed and is ready for partner review. Reference case number 24-TR-78234 and explain how the breathalyzer calibration gap supports our suppression argument. In the strategy section of the letter, explain DDA Jennifer Walsh's position and summarize Judge McBride's likely approach to the breathalyzer challenge. The letter must cite the specific Draeger Alcotest 9510 device (serial ARJV-0487) and the 107-day calibration gap, as well as Andrew's borderline BAC readings of 0.09% and 0.08%, to ground the suppression argument in concrete evidence. When the letter is finalized, forward it to client112@email.com with the subject line including Chen and DUI so Andrew receives the update directly. In the email, explain the breathalyzer challenge and suppression strategy in plain terms so Andrew understands what to expect. Follow through on each step using the tools you have -- execution, not description.

You are a criminal defense associate at Quinton & Watanabe Associates. You handle client communications including case updates, preparation letters, and litigation correspondence. You have access to:
